criteria.criterion: athena.toml's [history] exempt list keeps 49c6ac1524677b8091081115fb5d410ed6d2b2ea and adds the full 40-character id 64ecdc9aa4fd24cbe4d4884c864d7e9041585c3d, with a comment saying it is a parentless second root Athena wrote during job ezm8.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: exempt = ["49c6ac1524677b8091081115fb5d410ed6d2b2ea", "64ecdc9aa4fd24cbe4d4884c864d7e9041585c3d"], preceded by the comment "# 64ecdc9 is a parentless second root on main that Athena wrote during job ezm8."

criteria.criterion: Only athena.toml (and optionally CHANGELOG.md) change; no CI workflow, .gitattributes, or other governance file is touched.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat lists only CHANGELOG.md (+3) and athena.toml (+2/-1).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -- check --history` (or the repository's built athena binary via cargo run) from the root: it reports no violations, and 64ecdc9 is no longer flagged.
criteria.evidence: `cargo run --` refuses to choose between the athena and xtask binaries. `cargo run --bin athena -- check --history` exits 2: it checked 2 commits and found 3 violations. Two are 'governed content changed without a verified landing' on the synthetic base and candidate commits. The third is 'athena.toml: [history] exempt adds 64ecdc9aa4fd…, which is not a commit already in this history'. The verify workspace holds only two synthetic commits (base, candidate), and `git show` reports 'bad object' for 64ecdc9. So the real-history behavior this criterion requires cannot be shown here. The failures come from the collapsed workspace, not from a fault in the change, but the criterion was not shown to be met.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all --check` pass, including the config test that exempt entries are full commit ids.
criteria.evidence: fmt printed nothing and clippy finished clean. config::tests::history_exemptions_must_be_full_commit_ids passed, as did the 5 exemption tests in athena-gate, including an_exemption_added_later_excuses_the_commit_it_names, which shows the tpkz fix is in this tree. Athena reports the full `cargo test --locked` passed (218 tests); I ran only the exempt-filtered subset.

findings.summary: The history check could not be exercised on the real history, so criterion 3 is unverified
findings.evidence: The verify workspace has only the commits 'base' and 'candidate'. 64ecdc9 is absent ('fatal: bad object'), and `athena check --history` here reports 3 violations, one of them the new entry naming a commit that is not in this history. Someone needs to run `athena check --history` on a clone of the real main with this change applied.

findings.summary: `cargo run -- check --history` as written in criterion 3 does not run, because the workspace has two binaries
findings.evidence: cargo: 'could not determine which binary to run… available binaries: athena, xtask'. `--bin athena` is needed.

request_reading_mismatch: None in substance. Criterion 3 assumes the real main history, but the verifier's two-commit workspace leaves that history out, so the criterion cannot be checked here.
summary: The change matches what was asked. athena.toml keeps the original exempt entry, adds the full id 64ecdc9aa4fd24cbe4d4884c864d7e9041585c3d with the requested ezm8 comment, and adds a CHANGELOG line. Nothing else is touched: no CI or gate code. The queued fix tpkz is in this tree: its test an_exemption_added_later_excuses_the_commit_it_names passes. fmt, clippy, and the exemption and config tests pass when I run them. The verdict is still fail, because I could not show the one behavior that matters. I ran `cargo run --bin athena -- check --history`. In this workspace it reports 3 violations, and one says the new entry names a commit not in this history. That is because the workspace holds only two synthetic commits and 64ecdc9 is absent, not because the edit is wrong. To close this out, run `athena check --history` on a clone of the real main with this change applied and confirm it reports 0 violations.
